Lecture 2 · Compactness, connectedness and gluing

Self-check.

Prove that S1\sphere1S1 and [0,1][0,1][0,1] are not homeomorphic by removing one point. Explain why deleting an endpoint of the interval is not a useful test.

Show answer

Answer.

Delete the midpoint of [0,1][0,1][0,1]. The two resulting half-intervals give a separation. Deleting any point from the circle leaves a space homeomorphic to R\RR. Rotate that point to the north pole, then use Lecture 1’s stereographic projection. The line is path-connected by straight segments. A homeomorphism would restrict to a homeomorphism between these two punctured spaces, which is impossible. Deleting an endpoint leaves a path-connected half-open interval, so connectedness would not distinguish them.

Lecture 3 · Homotopy and the fundamental group

Self-check.

State in one sentence what the fundamental group of (X,x0)(X,x_0)(X,x0​) is and why we introduced it. Explain why paths themselves are replaced by classes.

Show answer

Answer.

The fundamental group is the group of endpoint-fixed homotopy classes of loops at x0x_0x0​, introduced to distinguish loops that cannot deform into one another while retaining concatenation. The two bracketings of three paths have different timings, but a change of timing is an endpoint-fixed homotopy. Thus associativity holds for classes.

Send [(γ,δ)][(\gamma,\delta)][(γ,δ)] to (wind⁡γ,wind⁡δ)∈Z2(\wind\gamma,\wind\delta)\in\Z^2(windγ,windδ)∈Z2. Projecting a product homotopy gives endpoint-fixed homotopies of the coordinates. Winding is invariant under these, so the map is well-defined. Projection respects concatenation, so the map preserves multiplication coordinatewise. Conversely, the component test of Lecture 1 makes a pair of loops a loop in the product, and a pair of endpoint-fixed homotopies a homotopy in the product. Lecture 4 · Covering spaces and rotations

Self-check.

State in one sentence what a covering map is and why we introduced it to study loop classes. Explain why specifying one starting point upstairs is essential.

Show answer

Answer.

A covering map is a continuous surjection with disjoint local inverse sheets, introduced to lift paths and homotopies and to recover loop classes from their endpoints when the covering space is simply connected. The initial point selects a sheet on the first subinterval. Each successive endpoint selects the next sheet, which is the decisive step in path-lift existence and uniqueness.

Lecture 6 · Homology and the Euler characteristic

Self-check.

Compute the Euler characteristic of the sphere from the boundary of a tetrahedron and from the boundary of an octahedron. Confirm the tetrahedral answer from the homology of its boundary.

Show answer

Answer.

The tetrahedron has four vertices. Every pair is an edge, giving (42)=6\binom42=6(24​)=6 edges, and every triple is a face, giving four triangles. The count is 4−6+4=24-6+4=24−6+4=2. The octahedron has vertices at the positive and negative coordinate-axis unit vectors. Every vertex joins the four vertices other than itself and its opposite, giving 6⋅4/2=126\cdot4/2=126⋅4/2=12 edges. A face chooses one endpoint from each axis, giving 23=82^3=823=8 triangles. Its count is 6−12+8=26-12+8=26−12+8=2, in agreement with the tetrahedron. The tetrahedral boundary has real Betti numbers (1,0,1)(1,0,1)(1,0,1), so its homological alternating sum is also 1−0+1=21-0+1=21−0+1=2.

Lecture 8 · Tangent spaces, Lie groups and homogeneous spaces

Self-check.

State in one sentence what a tangent vector is and why we introduced it. Then describe a point of TS1\tangentbundle\sphere1TS1 and what its projection retains.

Show answer

Answer.

A tangent vector is a class of curves through one point with the same coordinate velocity, introduced to define velocity without an ambient space. The chain rule makes equality of those velocities independent of the chart. A point of TS1\tangentbundle\sphere1TS1 is a circle position together with one tangent velocity there. The projection retains the position.

Lecture 9 · Vector fields and flows

Self-check.

State in one sentence what the Lie algebra of an abstract Lie group is and why left-invariant fields enter its definition.

The Lie algebra is TeGT_{\groupidentity}\LiegroupTe​G with the bracket [A,B]=[AL,BL](e)[A,B]=[A^L,B^L](\groupidentity)[A,B]=[AL,BL](e), obtained by extending tangent vectors by left translation so that their vector-field bracket is defined. Lecture 10 · Differential forms

Self-check.

State in one sentence what a differential kkk-form is and why it is introduced. Explain why repeated tangent arguments give zero.

Show answer

Answer.

A differential kkk-form is a smooth alternating multilinear measurement of kkk tangent vectors at each point, introduced as an integrand for signed kkk-dimensional integration. Exchanging two equal arguments leaves the value unchanged and negates it, so the value is zero.

Lecture 13 · De Rham cohomology

Self-check.

State what a de Rham cohomology class is and why we introduced it. Explain how a nonzero period distinguishes a class from zero.

Show answer

Answer.

A class is a closed form modulo addition of exact forms. In positive degree, the zero class consists of forms with a global primitive. We introduced the quotient to measure the obstruction to such a primitive. Stokes makes every period of an exact form zero, so a nonzero period proves that a closed form represents a nonzero class.

Lecture 14 · Degree, Poincaré–Hopf and de Rham’s theorem

Self-check.

Show answer

Answer.

For a smooth map between nonempty closed connected oriented manifolds of the same positive dimension, degree is the homotopy-invariant signed count of inverse images at a regular value expressed by integrating the pullback of a top form normalized to integral one. Lecture 25 · Topological band theory

Self-check.

Explain why the QWZ lower-band number is zero at u=3u=3u=3, without counting preimages.

Show answer

Answer.

The component dz=3+cos⁡kx+cos⁡kyd_z=3+\cos k_x+\cos k_ydz​=3+coskx​+cosky​ is at least one. Thus the direction map lies in the northern hemisphere and contracts there to the north pole. Its degree is zero by Lecture 14’s homotopy invariance.

Lecture 25 · Topological band theory

Self-check.

State in one sentence what the band Chern number is and why it was introduced. Explain why a nonzero value prevents a smooth periodic unit eigenvector.

Show answer

Answer.

The band Chern number is the integer normalized curvature flux of an isolated eigenline over the momentum torus, introduced to classify gapped bands and determine their filled-band Hall response. A global periodic eigenvector would make A\BerryconnA global, so Stokes on the closed torus would force that flux to vanish.

Lecture 26 · Higher homotopy groups and topological defects

Self-check.

State in one sentence what πn(X,x0)\pi_n(X,x_0)πn​(X,x0​) is and why we introduced it for defects.

Show answer

Answer.

The group πn(X,x0)\pi_n(X,x_0)πn​(X,x0​) consists of based homotopy classes of based maps Sn→XS^n\to XSn→X, so it records whether a linking sphere map can contract while its image basepoint stays fixed. A nonzero class obstructs extension over the transverse disk.

Lecture 26 · Higher homotopy groups and topological defects

Self-check.

An ordered medium has M=SO(3)\mathcal M=\SO(3)M=SO(3). Choose the linking domain in three-dimensional space. Find its local line classes and the result of joining two nontrivial lines.

Show answer

Answer.

The linking domain is a circle transverse to the line. Lecture 4 gives π1(SO(3))=Z2\pi_1(\SO(3))=\Z_2π1​(SO(3))=Z2​. It is abelian, so there are two free line classes. The sum of two nontrivial classes is zero, removing this local topological obstruction. This does not assert that a particular physical evolution makes the defects annihilate.

Lecture 26 · Higher homotopy groups and topological defects

Self-check.

A nematic configuration has two point defects. Chosen comparison paths give lifted degrees 333 and −2-2−2 at a common basepoint. Find the total based charge and its free label. Repeat when only the second path is changed by the nontrivial director loop. Explain why the local labels 333 and 222 do not determine a total free label.

Show answer

Answer.

The first total is 3+(−2)=13+(-2)=13+(−2)=1, with free label 111. The changed path acts by the target antipodal map, so the second representative becomes +2+2+2. The new total is 3+2=53+2=53+2=5, with free label 555. The same local absolute values have lost the comparison-path information.

Lecture 27 · Solitons and topological charge

Self-check.

For the scalar kink model, list the possible values of Q=(ϕ+−ϕ−)/(2v)\topcharge=(\phi_+-\phi_-)/(2v)Q=(ϕ+​−ϕ−​)/(2v) for vacuum endpoints. Count the ordered endpoint sectors and decide whether the charge distinguishes all of them.

Show answer

Answer.

The four ordered pairs are (−v,−v)(-v,-v)(−v,−v), (−v,+v)(-v,+v)(−v,+v), (+v,−v)(+v,-v)(+v,−v) and (+v,+v)(+v,+v)(+v,+v). Their charges are respectively zero, +1+1+1, −1-1−1 and zero. The two equal-endpoint pairs are different sectors because a continuous vacuum-valued endpoint cannot move between the disconnected vacua. Thus the charge is an invariant, but is not a complete label of the sector.

Lecture 27 · Solitons and topological charge

Self-check.

State in one sentence what a static soliton is and why we introduced its energy. Explain why a nonzero charge is insufficient to identify one.

Show answer

Answer.

A static soliton is a localized finite-energy stationary field, and its energy distinguishes stationary profiles and sector minima among fields with the same boundary topology. A charge labels allowed deformations, whereas the field equation must still be satisfied.

Lecture 28 · The index on the sphere

Self-check.

For n=0n=0n=0, determine the sphere index and both zero-mode counts. Explain what follows from the index alone.

Show answer

Answer.

The sphere theorem gives index zero and both kernel dimensions zero. The index alone says only that the two dimensions agree. Their vanishing uses the sphere-specific polynomial and Serre-duality count.

Lecture 28 · The index on the sphere

Self-check.

State in one sentence what the chiral index is and why we introduced it.

Show answer

Answer.

The chiral index is the difference of the complex zero-mode dimensions, introduced because positive squared-Dirac eigenvalues pair across chiralities and only the zero modes can leave an imbalance. The surface index theorem identifies that difference with the curvature integer.
